transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because for a long time now, I just wake up already feeling low. It's like... there’s this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic for work. And it pretty much just follows me through the whole day.
How long have you been waking up with this low feeling?

It's been going on for about two years and two months now. It started right around the time the staffing changed at the clinic where I work... my schedule started rotating all over the place, and, well, it's just been like this ever since.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I don't really know, honestly. I mean... I haven't really thought about it, so I'm not sure if I do or not. I just haven't really noticed.
Do you find yourself enjoying things as much as you used to?

Like I said, I really haven't paid much attention to it. I just go to work, come home, and try to get through the day. I don't think I really enjoy things the same way, but it's hard to say for sure since I haven't really been doing much besides working.
Can you think of anything you've done recently that you would say you truly enjoyed?

I honestly can't think of anything. Like I said, I just... I haven't really been doing anything besides working and coming home. So, no, I can't really think of a specific time recently where I felt like I truly enjoyed something.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about?

I guess so. Um... I just don't really think about the stuff I used to care about anymore. Like I was saying, my routine is pretty much just work and sleep now. So... yeah, I suppose the interest just isn't there, but I haven't really been keeping track of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the past two years?

No, not really. I mean, I still eat when I'm supposed to. I haven't noticed myself eating way more or way less than usual. It's just... food is just food. I eat to get through the day, but my appetite itself hasn't really changed.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past two years?

No, my sleep has been pretty much the same. I mean, I sleep fine. Like I mentioned, my routine is mostly just working and sleeping, so... I definitely get enough sleep. I haven't noticed any real changes with it, like having trouble falling asleep or waking up a bunch. It's just normal, I guess.
Do you often feel tired or have low energy?

Yeah, pretty much all the time. Even after I have a day off or, you know, get to sleep late, my body just still feels completely worn out. By the time I finish my shift at work—rooming patients, catching up on all the charts—it just feels like I have absolutely nothing left in the tank. I don't have the energy to do laundry, or shoot hoops, or even mess around with my electronics stuff like I used to. I'm just drained.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless?

No, not really. I don't think I feel guilty about anything, and I wouldn't say I feel worthless. I'm just... tired all the time. But I don't really have those kinds of thoughts about myself. I just go to work and do my job, so I don't feel like I'm doing anything wrong.
Do you ever have days where you wake up feeling okay, or is the low feeling always there?

No, the low feeling is pretty much always there. Honestly, that's why I came in... for a long time now, I wake up and I already feel low. It's like there's this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get out of bed or head to the clinic. And it just... it pretty much follows me through the whole day. There really aren't any okay days.
Have you had periods in the past two years where your low mood significantly improved for a while before returning?
No, not really. It hasn't ever really lifted. For the last couple of years, it's just been a constant thing. I haven't had any breaks from it where I felt better for a while. It's just always there.
Can you think of any periods, even if they were brief, where your mood felt significantly better than it does on most days?

No, I really can't. Like I said, it's just been a constant low. I can't remember a time in the last two years where I felt significantly better, even for a little bit. It's just always the same heavy feeling.
Do you notice that your low mood tends to worsen or improve at specific times of the year?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. It's just... it's the same all year round. Winter, summer, it doesn't seem to make a difference. It's just always there.
Do you think your low mood is related to any particular time of year or season?
Like I just mentioned, no, I don't think so. It doesn't change with the seasons. It's just a constant thing, no matter what time of year it is.
Has this low feeling been present for most of every day, for the entire two years and two months you've been experiencing it?

Yeah, pretty much every single day. It's been exactly like that for about two years and two months now. It all really started back when the staffing changed at the clinic where I work... they had my schedule rotating all over the place, and ever since then, it's just been this constant low, most of the day, every day.
Has this low feeling lasted for two years continuously without any breaks?

Yeah, it's been continuous. Like I was saying, it's been about two years and two months straight, without any real breaks. Ever since they changed the staffing at the clinic and started messing with my schedule, it's just been this same feeling every day.
Has there been a period of at least two weeks where you didn't feel this low during the past two years?
No, there hasn't. Like I said, it's just been constant. I haven't had a break from it for even a couple of days, let alone two weeks. It's just always there.
Has your low mood lasted for two years or more without any significant improvement?

Yeah, like I mentioned, there hasn't been any improvement at all. It's been going on for about two years and two months now, ever since the clinic staffing changed and my schedule started rotating all over the place. It's just stayed like this the whole time.
